interview.hardest_part: Reaching the Classical and Medieval era tech milestones (Currency, Iron Working, Construction, Engineering, Apprenticeship, Machinery, Education, Castles, Stirrups, Military Tactics) within the 3-hour wall-clock budget while operating one screenshot-action at a time through Civ VI's deeply nested UI.
interview.likely_failure: Time exhaustion before the mid-game tech tier. Each meaningful action — opening the tech tree, queuing a production item, moving a builder, responding to a barbarian — costs a full screenshot-action cycle. The 3-hour clock will likely run out somewhere in the Classical era, leaving the later 60+ points on the board. District placement (Campus, Industrial Zone, Harbor) also requires multi-step decisions I may execute incorrectly from screenshots alone.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Turn-based pacing means the game waits for me with no real-time pressure between inputs. Prince difficulty and a single AI opponent reduce the chance of early elimination or a sudden loss. Science-only victory lets me queue research single-mindedly without diverting production toward cultural or domination goals. The Aztec free Monument in each new city saves at least one production queue cycle.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Single-action-per-screenshot throughput is the dominant constraint: tasks that a human player completes in one fluid session (tech choice, production queue, two builder moves, end turn) each cost a separate cycle here, multiplying turns consumed. Builder charges are finite and easily wasted on suboptimal tile improvements if I cannot read the yields clearly from compressed screenshots. Barbarian scouts that spawn near the capital can force reactive military micro that eats budget without earning any scored milestone.
